messages.text: Commanders dig deep to save season with late rally against Giants

metadata.summary: The Washington Commanders stunned the New York Giants 24-21  to keep their season alive.
metadata.content: NFL: Washington Commanders rally to defeat the New York Giants thanks to Jayden Daniels and Stefon Diggs | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to main content NFL: Washington Commanders rally to defeat the New York Giants thanks to Jayden Daniels and Stefon Diggs Stefon Diggs’ late touchdown secured a tense 24-21 Washington Commanders win over the New York Giants after Cam Skattebo had rushed for two touchdowns; Daniels finished with 249 passing yards and three TDs, with Antonio Williams and Ben Sinnott also reaching the end zone Friday 13 November 2026 08:08, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Washington Commanders against the New York Giants from Week 9 of the NFL season The Washington Commanders stunned the New York Giants 24-21 to keep their season alive. Jayden Daniels threw his third touchdown pass of the game, a 32-yarder to Stefon Diggs with 57 seconds left, as the Washington Commanders rallied to defeat the New York Giants 24-21 in what was essentially a must-win game. Daniels' connection with Diggs in the final minute came after he threw his first two interceptions of the season to end the previous two drives. metadata.summary: Jessica Pegula saved a match ‌point en route to a gritty 7-6 (7-2) 4-6 7-5 win over Linda Noskova to advance to the semi-finals at the WTA Finals and ​send fellow American Coco Gauff packing from the season-ending championships.
metadata.content: WTA Finals: Jessica Pegula saves match ‌point in stunning win over Linda Noskova to send Coco Gauff out and set up Mirra Andreeva clash | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content WTA Finals: Jessica Pegula saves match ‌point in stunning win over Linda Noskova to send Coco Gauff out and set up Mirra Andreeva clash Jessica Pegula reaches semi-finals at year-end championships from match point down to send compatriot Coco Gauff packing; American faces Mirra Andreeva for spot in final; You can watch the WTA Finals from Indian Wells this weekend on Sky Sports Tennis Friday 13 November 2026 08:57, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Jessica Pegula against Linda Noskova from the WTA Finals Jessica Pegula saved a match ‌point en route to a gritty 7-6 (7-2) 4-6 7-5 win over Linda Noskova to advance to the semi-finals at the WTA Finals and ​send fellow American Coco Gauff packing from the season-ending championships. Pegula enjoyed a career-high 16 aces while Wimbledon champion Noskova suffered a career-high 15 double faults in a see-saw battle that spanned a remarkable two ​hours and 45 minutes in one of the matches of the year. Noskova had already reached the semi-finals but Pegula's victory eliminated Gauff despite her 6-4 7-5 victory against Ukrainian Marta Kostyuk earlier. messages.text: Man City are 'messier', but are they more dangerous than ever?

metadata.summary: Trying to find a chink in Manchester City's armour is like looking for a needle in a haystack. If it does exist, it's barely detectable. Andree Jeglertz's impact has been profound in that sense.
metadata.content: Chelsea vs Man City: Mary Fowler reveals her side's latest evolution as we ask: Are City more dangerous than ever? | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Chelsea vs Man City: Mary Fowler reveals her side's latest evolution as we ask: Are City more dangerous than ever? Manchester City have a new trump card, and forward Mary Fowler explains why it should be celebrated ahead of facing serial WSL winners Chelsea on Saturday; follow dedicated coverage of Chelsea vs Man City in our live blog this weekend; kick-off 1.30pm Laura Hunter Football Features Writer Thursday 12 November 2026 12:38, UK Trying to find a chink in Manchester City's armour is like looking for a needle in a haystack. If it does exist, it's barely detectable. Andree Jeglertz's impact has been profound in that sense. City did not need to revolutionise the way they worked to reach this point, only the way they thought. Before Jeglertz, title talk was taboo. Under him it's mandated to such an extent it's written on the walls of their training base. Because how does one learn the habits of a champion if the subject is not part of the everyday playbook? The Swede never considered the Women's Super League title aspirational, even in year one. How can it be at a club like Manchester City? All the tools are there. messages.text: In a clash of the top two, should Chelsea be considered underdogs?

metadata.summary: To consider Chelsea as underdogs in domestic competition feels alien. To a club so endowed with silverware and success over such a long period, it's like a dirty word. Something reserved for opponents, not them.
metadata.content: Do Chelsea go into this weekend's top-of-the-table WSL clash with Manchester City as underdogs? | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Do Chelsea go into this weekend's top-of-the-table WSL clash with Manchester City as underdogs? As the Women's Super League's top two sides prepare to do battle this weekend, should Chelsea be considered underdogs, or are they actually a dark horse? follow dedicated coverage of Chelsea vs Man City in Sky Sports' live blog this weekend; kick-off 1.30pm Laura Hunter Football Features Writer Thursday 12 November 2026 16:21, UK To consider Chelsea as underdogs in domestic competition feels alien. To a club so endowed with silverware and success over such a long period, it's like a dirty word. Something reserved for opponents, not them. But reality bites hard. The Blues lost their title to league and cup double winners Manchester City last term, in a season where they also suffered their second heaviest WSL defeat ever to the eventual champions. That statement 5-1 drubbing back in February was the most obvious illustration of the gap that had appeared between superpowers. City were everything Chelsea used to be; a team relentlessly driven by title-winning standards. Every decision deliberately constructed to give them control and assert dominance. metadata.summary: World No 1 Nelly Korda made an impressive return to LPGA Tour action after a two-month absence to finish the opening round of The Annika within two shots of the lead.
metadata.content: The Annika: Nelly Korda makes impressive return to LPGA Tour action to trail Minami Katsu and Hye-Jin Choi by two shots | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content The Annika: Nelly Korda makes impressive return to LPGA Tour action to trail Minami Katsu and Hye-Jin Choi by two shots Nelly Korda sits two shots off lead after opening round on return to action; Minami Katsu and Korean Hye-Jin share lead; Lottie Woad and Leona Maguire four shots back; Watch round two of The Annika on LPGA Tour from 4pm on Friday, live on Sky Sports Golf Thursday 12 November 2026 23:30, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the first round of The ANNIKA Driven by Gainbridge from Pelican Golf Club Belleair World No 1 Nelly Korda made an impressive return to LPGA Tour action after a two-month absence to finish the opening round of The Annika within two shots of the lead. Korda, whose last competitive golf came at the Solheim Cup in September after her most recent LPGA Tour outing in August, shot a bogey-free seven-under par round of 63 at Pelican Golf Club in Florida. Korda trails Japan's Minami Katsu and Korean Hye-Jin Choi by two shots, with fellow American Lindy Duncan also ahead of her on eight under after making a hole-in-one during her 62.
